title: sse: fix streaming chunking & framing for partial JSON, delimiter bugs, and token/event ordering
author: Asha Patel
commit_summary: 3 commits: 1) add robust chunk boundary detection and delimiter normalization in stream_buffer; 2) update sse_handler to preserve token/event ordering and backpressure signals; 3) compatibility and tests for OpenAI-style SSE event sequences;
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming framing bugs: robust handling of partial JSON across chunks, normalized delimiters, preserved token/event ordering, and improved final DONE emission. No breaking API changes.
description:
Context & motivation:
Customers (internal and external) reported intermittent JSON parse failures and malformed events when streaming long structured outputs via our OpenAI-compatibility SSE layer. Root causes included: inconsistent newline/delimiter mixes from different model backends, partial JSON objects split across chunk boundaries, and the handler applying framing heuristics that could reorder or drop token fragments during backpressure. These bugs surface as partial JSON objects (e.g. {"tool_call": {"name": "send"}}) split across events, extra empty data events, and occasional reordering when buffering was flushed during autoscaling or connection retries.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a stream_buffer module with deterministic chunk boundary detection and delimiter normalization (LF, CRLF, mixed).
- Changes sse_handler framing to buffer incomplete JSON objects until a complete JSON token/object is available or a soft timeout is reached.
- Preserves strict token/event ordering: tokens are reassembled in the original emission order before any downstream processing or SSE flush.
- Adds heuristics to prevent emitting spurious empty data events and to correctly emit the final 'data: [DONE]' event without losing trailing tokens.
- Adds extensive unit and integration tests that simulate interleaved delimiters, partial JSON splits, network chunking, and backpressure-induced flushes.
- Small OpenAI-compat wrapper adjustments to accept repaired framing and to surface a single unified event stream to SDKs.

Files & key changes (high level):
- redwood/serve/runtime/stream_buffer.py: new module implementing a small-state machine for chunk assembly, delimiter normalization, and soft-flush timers. Includes comments describing invariants (order, idempotence).
- redwood/serve/runtime/sse_handler.py: updated to use stream_buffer APIs. Reworked framing loop so we only call into JSON parsing code when a complete JSON object or top-level token boundary is seen. Backpressure hooks preserved and now thread-safe.
- redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py: compatibility layer tolerates mixed delimiter streams and no longer assumes events align to token boundaries.
- redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streams.py: small change to the high-level consumer to handle delayed finalization of the streaming iterator (await the buffer soft-timer when needed).
- redwood/tests/test_sse_streaming.py: new tests covering partial JSON across chunks, mixed CRLF/LF, delayed DONE semantics, and ordering under simulated backpressure.
- docs and promql: updated docs to call out improvements and added a metric to track streaming reassemblies and framing retries.

Implementation notes / heuristics:
- Delimiter normalization: every incoming byte chunk is normalized to a canonical '\n' on ingress. We keep original offsets for diagnostics but operate on normalized streams to avoid CRLF/LF mismatches.
- JSON reassembly: we use a small stack-based check for top-level braces/brackets to detect complete objects/arrays across chunks. For top-level token streams (tokenized assistant output), we fall back to newline-delimited token frames.
- Soft-timeout behavior: if a partial JSON message remains unclosed for more than 250ms but no additional bytes arrive, we attempt a conservative emit if it parses as a recoverable fragment; otherwise we emit an annotated error event and close the stream. This prevents users from seeing indefinite stalls while preserving correctness in the common case.
- Order guarantees: the buffer tracks sequence positions and ensures flushes are processed FIFO. When backpressure triggers a partial flush, we attach a 'partial' marker internally so the consumer can rehydrate correctly.

Testing & CI:
- Local unit tests cover ~25 scenarios (edge cases included). Integration harness simulates network chunking and a mischievous model that inserts '\r\n' and '\n' randomly.
- CI initially failed due to a race in the soft-timer cancelation (flaky test); fixed by making cancelation idempotent and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, mypy).

Review conversation (high-level):
- Jamal: requested stronger invariants comments and an explicit test for the 'data: [DONE]' trailing case.
- Author (Asha): added tests and comments, clarified the soft-timeout tradeoff in PR description.
- Liu: suggested moving the delimiter normalization earlier in the pipeline to reduce duplicate logic; author did a small refactor to centralize normalization in stream_buffer.
- Marta: requested a docs blurb and a metric; both added.
- Approvals: Jamal and Liu approved after changes; Marta approved after docs update.

Rollout plan / backports:
- This is safe to roll to hosted immediately. For Dedicated & Private: deploy in a phased rollout with canary (10%) to verify no regressions on heavy-traffic customers.
- Backports: cherrypick to release/2026-02 for customers on the hotfix branch. Patch PR prepared (will open after merge).

Observability:
- Added metric 'streaming.reassembly.count' (increment on every reassembly event) and 'streaming.reassembly.latency_ms' to detect increased fragmentation. Dashboards updated in observability pack.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Evaluate whether the soft-timeout should be adaptive based on observed packet inter-arrival times (ENG-1301).
- Consider exposing an opt-in relaxed-framing mode for extremely high-throughput pipelines that can tolerate partial JSON reassembly at the SDK layer.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added (network chunking harness)
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Metrics added
- [x] Reviewed and approved
- [x] Changelog/release notes entry added

CI summary: initial run - one flaky test failing due to timer race; fixed in second commit. Final CI: all checks passing.

Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-27.

Notes for infra / on-call: if a customer still reports a parsing failure, ask for a raw captured byte-stream (we added diagnostic hooks that can be toggled with a debug flag) and file under SUP-452.
